findings.title: Submit button is a div with click handler and is not keyboard accessible
findings.reason: The element has a pointer click listener but is not focusable and does not appear in the keyboard focus sequence, so keyboard users cannot activate it.
findings.who_is_affected: Keyboard-only users, switch access users, and screen reader users cannot submit the form because the submit control is unreachable by Tab.
findings.how_to_fix: Replace the div with a native button element, or add tabindex="0", a role="button", and a keydown handler for Enter and Space.

findings.title: Keyboard focus is permanently trapped in the terms section
findings.reason: Tab key cycles only between #terms-first and #terms-last; #agree and a link are unreachable and no Escape exit is provided.
findings.who_is_affected: Keyboard-only users become permanently stuck in the terms section and cannot reach the agree checkbox or any later interactive element.
findings.how_to_fix: Remove the preventDefault() calls from the keydown Tab handlers in quiz-signup.js so focus follows the natural DOM order.

findings.title: Page auto-redirects after 300 seconds with no user control
findings.reason: A meta refresh tag forces navigation to course.html after 300 seconds without offering the user a way to turn off, adjust, or extend the time limit.
findings.who_is_affected: People with cognitive or motor disabilities who need more time to complete the form may lose their data when the page redirects.
findings.how_to_fix: Remove the meta http-equiv="refresh" tag and implement server-side session expiry with a warning dialog instead.

findings.title: Custom checkbox is missing the required aria-checked attribute
findings.reason: The element has role="checkbox" but no aria-checked attribute; JavaScript only toggles a CSS class and never updates the ARIA state.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users cannot tell whether the agree checkbox is checked or unchecked because its ARIA state is never exposed.
findings.how_to_fix: Set aria-checked="false" on the element initially and toggle it to "true" / "false" in the click handler in quiz-signup.js.

findings.title: Close-terms button has no accessible name
findings.reason: The icon-only button contains an SVG with aria-hidden="true" and has no aria-label, title, or visible text.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users cannot identify or activate the button because it has no accessible name.
findings.how_to_fix: Add aria-label="Close terms" to the button element.

findings.title: Email input has no associated label
findings.reason: The email input has no explicit label element, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no title, and no placeholder; screen readers cannot announce the field purpose.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users cannot determine what data to enter in this field.
findings.how_to_fix: Replace the span with <label for="email">Email</label> so the input is programmatically associated with its visible label.

findings.title: Display name field has an invalid autocomplete value
findings.reason: The autocomplete attribute value "nick-name" is not a recognized token; the valid token is "nickname" (no hyphen).
findings.who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities and motor impairments who rely on browser autofill cannot use it on this field.
findings.how_to_fix: Change autocomplete="nick-name" to autocomplete="nickname".

findings.title: Hint text fails minimum color contrast
findings.reason: Hint text has a contrast ratio of 2.81 against its white background; the required minimum for normal text at 14.4px is 4.5:1.
findings.who_is_affected: People with low vision or color blindness cannot read the hint text "We only use this to send your quiz link."
findings.how_to_fix: Darken the hint color to at least #767676 on a white background to achieve 4.5:1 contrast.

findings.title: Custom radio button has no visible focus indicator
findings.reason: The engine confirmed that the radio input's outline, box-shadow, border, background, color, and underline are identical with and without keyboard focus.
findings.who_is_affected: Keyboard users cannot tell which radio button is currently focused.
findings.how_to_fix: Replace the .level-radio:focus-visible { outline: none; } rule with a visible focus style such as a box-shadow or outline with at least 3:1 contrast against the surrounding color.

findings.title: Help about levels button is too small to activate
findings.reason: The button is 16x16 CSS pixels with a safe clickable diameter of only 8px; the minimum is 24x24px.
findings.who_is_affected: People with limited motor control and touch screen users cannot reliably activate the small button.
findings.how_to_fix: Increase .help-icon width and height to at least 24px, or add sufficient padding to bring the safe click area to 24px.

findings.title: Help about timing button is too small to activate
findings.reason: The button is 16x16 CSS pixels with a safe clickable diameter of only 8px; the minimum is 24x24px.
findings.who_is_affected: People with limited motor control and touch screen users cannot reliably activate the small button.
findings.how_to_fix: Increase .help-icon width and height to at least 24px, or add sufficient padding to bring the safe click area to 24px.

findings.title: HTML element is missing a lang attribute
findings.reason: The html element has no lang attribute, so assistive technologies cannot select the correct voice or pronunciation rules.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users may hear the page content pronounced with the wrong language voice.
findings.how_to_fix: Add lang="en" to the html element.

findings.title: Badge image has a non-descriptive alt attribute
findings.reason: The badge image uses alt="image", which is not descriptive and does not convey the meaning of the Cell Explorer badge reward.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users hear the meaningless text "image" instead of understanding the badge's significance.
findings.how_to_fix: Change alt to a description such as "Cell Explorer badge" or use alt="" if the image is purely decorative and the caption text alone is sufficient.

findings.title: Email field label is a span, not a label element
findings.reason: A span with class field-name is used in place of a label element, so there is no programmatic association between the visible text "Email" and the input.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users hear the email field without a name, and people who click the label text cannot activate the input.
findings.how_to_fix: Replace Email with .

findings.title: Submit instruction uses color and position to identify the button
findings.reason: The instruction "press the green button on the right" relies solely on color and spatial position to identify the submit control.
findings.who_is_affected: Color-blind users and screen reader users cannot identify which control the instruction refers to.
findings.how_to_fix: Replace the instruction with "press the Sign up button" so it identifies the control by its label text.

findings.title: Custom radio buttons and fake checkbox may lack sufficient non-text contrast
findings.reason: Custom radio buttons and the fake checkbox use appearance:none with borders defined in CSS; their boundary contrast against adjacent background was not measured by the engine.
findings.who_is_affected: People with low vision may not perceive the boundaries of the custom radio buttons or checkbox.
findings.how_to_fix: Verify that the 2px border on .level-radio and .fake-checkbox has at least 3:1 contrast against the surrounding background and test with a contrast checker.

findings.title: Selecting a course option causes unexpected page navigation
findings.reason: Changing the course dropdown to maths or writing immediately navigates to index.html via window.location.href without any warning or confirmation.
findings.who_is_affected: Keyboard users and screen reader users may accidentally navigate away and lose form data when using arrow keys to browse options.
findings.how_to_fix: Remove the change-event navigation and instead show a note that only Biology basics is available on this page, or require a separate confirm button.

findings.title: Course select triggers navigation on input without user confirmation
findings.reason: The change event listener navigates away immediately when a non-Biology option is chosen; no prior warning is given.
findings.who_is_affected: Keyboard users and people with cognitive disabilities are disoriented by a page change caused only by selecting a dropdown value.
findings.how_to_fix: Remove the auto-navigation or wrap it in a confirmation dialog before redirecting.

findings.title: Form validation errors are not communicated in text
findings.reason: When email or date validation fails, the code adds an .invalid CSS class (red border and background) but provides no text error message.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users and blind users cannot perceive color-only error indicators and never learn which field is invalid or why.
findings.how_to_fix: Insert a text error message (e.g., via aria-describedby pointing to an error span) and set aria-invalid="true" on each invalid input.

findings.title: Email field has no programmatically associated label
findings.reason: The visible text "Email" is in a span rather than a label element, so the programmatic association required by this criterion is absent.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users and people with cognitive disabilities cannot reliably associate the label text with the input.
findings.how_to_fix: Replace the span with <label for="email">Email</label>.

findings.title: Date field has no format instruction
findings.reason: The date input requires a dd/mm/yyyy format (enforced by the JS regex) but shows no visible hint or placeholder about the expected format.
findings.who_is_affected: All users, especially people with cognitive disabilities, may enter dates in the wrong format and receive no guidance on what is expected.
findings.how_to_fix: Add a visible description or placeholder such as "DD/MM/YYYY" and link it with aria-describedby so screen readers can announce it.
